extracted.intended_audience: The people of the State of New York; voters and citizens considering ratification of the proposed U.S. Constitution
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and practical principles for designing a national constitution able to preserve the Union and execute national laws effectively (addressed to voters and framers). Emphasizes enforceability, division of powers, and institutional safeguards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legislation for individuals, not for states
rubrics_metrics.description: “The great and radical vice in the construction of the existing Confederation is in the principle of LEGISLATION for STATES or GOVERNMENTS, in their CORPORATE or COLLECTIVE CAPACITIES, and as contradistinguished from the INDIVIDUALS of which they consist.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Laws that operate only on states (collective bodies) are in practice mere recommendations because the Union cannot directly enforce them on individuals; to be effective, federal laws must extend to the persons of the citizens. The essay explains that legislation aimed at states creates a system where compliance is optional and enforcement depends on the states' goodwill.

rubrics_metrics.name: Laws must be attended with a sanction (penalty)
rubrics_metrics.description: “It is essential to the idea of a law, that it be attended with a sanction; or, in other words, a penalty or punishment for disobedience.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A rule without a penalty is advice. The text identifies the necessity of an enforceable sanction as part of the very idea of law and frames this as a standard for whether a government truly makes law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanction must be enforceable by courts or (if necessary) force; courts preferable for individual-directed laws
rubrics_metrics.description: “This penalty, whatever it may be, can only be inflicted in two ways: by the agency of the courts and ministers of justice, or by military force; by the COERCION of the magistracy, or by the COERCION of arms.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For laws addressed to individuals, ordinary magistracy and courts are the proper means of enforcement. Military coercion applies only to collective bodies and leads to grave dangers; therefore constitutional design should prefer enforcement through courts to secure compliance without resort to arms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal government must be empowered to act directly on citizens
rubrics_metrics.description: “We must resolve to incorporate into our plan those ingredients ... we must extend the authority of the Union to the persons of the citizens,--the only proper objects of government.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Union should not rely on intermediate state legislatures to give effect to national measures; it must be able to employ the ordinary magistrate to execute its own resolutions so that the national authority is manifested through the courts and addresses individuals directly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-compliance (omission) differs from direct resistance; constitution should minimize opportunities for evasive non-compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: “The plausibility of this objection will vanish the moment we advert to the essential difference between a mere NON-COMPLIANCE and a DIRECT and ACTIVE RESISTANCE.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If national laws operate directly on citizens, states cannot defeat them simply by refusing to act or by evasive measures. Design that enables direct operation on individuals forces states to choose open and plainly unconstitutional resistance, which is more visible and less likely to succeed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid requiring concurrence of numerous sovereign wills to execute measures
rubrics_metrics.description: “In our case, the concurrence of thirteen distinct sovereign wills is requisite, under the Confederation, to the complete execution of every important measure that proceeds from the Union.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requiring unanimous or near-unanimous agreement among many sovereign states produces paralysis: partial compliance, imitation of delinquency, and systemic failure. A constitution should reduce reliance on such multi-party concurrence for execution of national measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle of legislation for states is the 'parent of anarchy' and tends toward civil war
rubrics_metrics.description: “This exceptionable principle may, as truly as emphatically, be styled the parent of anarchy: It has been seen that delinquencies in the members of the Union are its natural and necessary offspring; and that whenever they happen, the only constitutional remedy is force, and the immediate effect of the use of it, civil war.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designs that leave the national government dependent on coercion of states invite faction, imbalance, and armed conflict. Historical confederacies that legislated for member bodies rather than for individuals experienced weakness, oppression, and war.

rubrics_metrics.name: A national government needing a standing army to enforce ordinary laws is impracticable and dangerous
rubrics_metrics.description: “It seems to require no pains to prove that the States ought not to prefer a national Constitution which could only be kept in motion by the instrumentality of a large army continually on foot to execute the ordinary requisitions or decrees of the government.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relying on military coercion to make the Union operate would require resources beyond the Union's means and would likely degenerate into military despotism. A workable constitution avoids placing ordinary enforcement on the sword.

rubrics_metrics.name: State governments' administration of civil and criminal justice gives them superior local influence
rubrics_metrics.description: “There is one transcendant advantage belonging to the province of the State governments ... I mean the ordinary administration of criminal and civil justice. This, of all others, is the most powerful, most universal, and most attractive source of popular obedience and attachment.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because local governments administer justice and daily concerns, they naturally command stronger popular loyalty and can serve as a counterweight to national power. Constitutional design should acknowledge this fact in allocating powers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate division of powers: national authority over commerce/finance/war; states retain local police and private justice
rubrics_metrics.description: “Commerce, finance, negotiation, and war seem to comprehend all the objects which have charms for minds governed by that passion; and all the powers necessary to those objects ought, in the first instance, to be lodged in the national depository. The administration of private justice ... all those things ... proper to be provided for by local legislation.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assigning national control of external and collective concerns (commerce, finance, foreign affairs, war) and leaving local, domestic matters to states reduces motives for federal usurpation and keeps local governance responsive to citizens' everyday needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not rely on sense of common interest among states; design must constrain human passions
rubrics_metrics.description: “They admit that the government of the United States is destitute of energy, they contend against conferring upon it those powers which are requisite to supply that energy... Why has government been instituted at all? Because the passions of men will not conform to the dictates of reason and justice, without constraint.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Experience shows that expecting states to comply out of goodwill is naive. Constitutional structures must provide binding mechanisms and enforcement (directly on individuals) because human self-interest and faction will otherwise defeat national measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal judiciary and informed public opinion as safeguards against unconstitutional state encroachment
rubrics_metrics.description: “If the judges were not embarked in a conspiracy with the legislature, they would pronounce the resolutions of such a majority to be contrary to the supreme law of the land, unconstitutional, and void. If the people were not tainted ... they ... would throw their weight into the national scale.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An independent judicial branch able to declare state acts unconstitutional and a sufficiently enlightened and engaged populace are essential checks that make direct federal legislation practicable and limit illegitimate state usurpation; conspiracies among judges or people can defeat these safeguards but are treated as less probable.
